insights.claim: The component implements a dual-plane architecture with a CRD-driven control plane and an Envoy ExtProc data plane, requiring Istio service mesh integration for external provider connectivity.
insights.reasoning: The ExternalProvider controller creates Istio ServiceEntry and DestinationRule resources alongside Kubernetes Services, establishing a hard dependency on Istio service mesh for external provider routing and TLS origination. This pattern couples the component to Istio-enabled clusters.

insights.claim: The ExtProc server is a hand-maintained fork of the upstream llm-d-inference-payload-processor runner, requiring manual synchronization when the upstream dependency is updated.
insights.reasoning: The source comments explicitly document that cmd/runner.go is a hand-maintained copy of the upstream runner required because upstream offers no hook to wrap the ext-proc server. The KEEP IN SYNC comment indicates ongoing maintenance burden when bumping the dependency version.

insights.claim: The ExtProc gRPC server uses self-signed certificates for optional TLS rather than integrating with a certificate management system, trading operational simplicity for certificate lifecycle management.
insights.reasoning: The newExtProcRunnable function generates a self-signed certificate at startup when secureServing is enabled. This avoids external cert-manager dependencies but means certificates are ephemeral and regenerated on each pod restart, which may complicate mTLS verification by upstream Envoy proxies.
